exposure: Enhanced programme of Surgical Site Infection (SSI) Infection Prevention and Control (IPC)
cohort: Adult patients undergoing coronary artery bypass graft, hip arthroplasty, or caesarean section in the UK National Health Service (NHS).
finding: Enhanced programs of Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) for Surgical Site Infections (SSIs) generally lead to lower costs and higher quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) compared to current measures, though this varies by surgery type and is sensitive to various factors.
mod_finding: The study included caesarean section as one of the three surgery types evaluated, finding that enhanced Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) for Surgical Site Infections (SSIs) may deliver improved health outcomes at a lower cost, though this consistency varies across surgery types.
